title: Teller Till, Branch Cash and Branch Day own physical custody evidence
summary: Teller Till and Branch Cash model physical counter/vault custody, while Branch Day certifies opening/closing from typed evidence. None owns customer balances or Ledger state.
invariants: Teller Till is not an ATM and does not own customer account or Ledger truth.
A bank transaction and a physical till movement are separate facts correlated by an orchestration boundary.
Branch Cash preserves released cash as explicit in-transit custody until another endpoint accepts it; cash cannot disappear into a generic transfer-failed state.
Branch Cash authority binds exact transfer semantics, independent checker approval, staff authority and policy result.
Branch Day coordinates evidence only; opening/closing is blocked by cash in transit, unresolved reconciliation or physical discrepancy.
Internal replenishment/skim/till-to-till movements are custody changes and net to zero at branch level.

provenance.claim: Teller Till owns physical custody, not customer/Ledger truth, and internal branch cash is separate from customer cash.
Branch Cash owns physical custody, in-transit state and exact-action authority envelope.
Branch Day coordinates typed physical evidence and blocks close on in-transit/discrepancy/reconciliation.
